clues.title: Plate: long white, blue EU strip on left
text: Latvian **licence plates** are long and white, with the standard blue European strip on the left.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Long white plates with the standard blue European strip on the left.

clues.title: Bollard: thin, slightly curved, numbered
text: Latvian bollards have a **thin, slightly curved shape**.

They have a rectangular reflector on the front, and two circular reflectors on the back. The reflectors can be white or orange. The black strip is slightly angled. Bollards often have numbers below the front reflector.
NOTE: Estonian and Lithuanian bollards look different.
!![This infographic](/images/latvia/nordics_bollards.png) shows the main similarities and differences between the bollards of the Baltic and Nordic countries.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Thin, slightly curved bollard with a rectangular reflector on the front and two round ones on the back, white or orange. Black strip is slightly angled, often with numbers below.

differs.how: Estonian bollards have a different shape
Lithuanian bollards have a different shape

clues.title: Pole: hook insulators alternating left-right
text: Latvian poles have distinctive poletops, with **hook-shaped insulators**, that are arranged in an alternating manner: left-right-left (or vice versa).
NOTE: These poletops are much more rare in the other two Baltic countries. They can however appear in some other European countries.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pole tops with hook-shaped insulators that alternate left, right, left. Much rarer in the other two Baltic countries, but seen in some other European countries.

clues.title: Chevron: white with red arrow
text: Latvia uses white chevrons with red arrows.
NOTE: Many other European countries, including Lithuania and Poland, use the same chevrons.
!!However, Estonia, Russia and Ukraine use chevrons with the opposite colour scheme: red with white arrows.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White chevrons with red arrows. Many European countries use these, including Lithuania and Poland. Estonia, Russia and Ukraine reverse it: red with white arrows.

clues.title: Marker: blue km post parallel to road
text: All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker. However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
In Latvia, the marker will be **parallel** to the road. It only has a number on one side.
For a quick overview of all three Baltic countries, see [this infographic](/images/latvia/baltics_kmmarkerinfographic.png).

images.caption: A blue kilometre post with '27' circled, beside a diagram showing it set parallel to the road

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: All three Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker. Here it sits parallel to the road and has a number on one side only.

differs.how: Marker sits at a different angle to the road
Marker sits at a different angle to the road

clues.title: Sign: thick red border with thin white outline
text: Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
Latvian signs have a **thick** red border, with a **thin white outline** around it.

images.caption: Baltic signs compared: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania no-stopping and yield signs, with border notes

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Warning and speed signs have a thick red border with a thin white line around it. Each Baltic country has a slightly different border.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, 5 stripes, long legs
text: Latvian pedestrian signs have **five stripes**, which is unique within the Baltics. Uniquely, the pedestrian has noticeably **long legs** compared to pedestrian signs in other European countries.
The other two Baltic countries have three stripes on their pedestrian signs.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The pedestrian sign has five stripes and a figure with noticeably long legs. The other two Baltic countries show three stripes.

clues.title: Sign: bus stop sign with 5 bus windows
text: Latvian bus stop signs have this design.
Most importantly, the bus has **five windows**. Within the Baltics, this is unique to Latvia. The other two Baltic countries have four windows.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The bus on the bus stop sign has five windows. The other Baltic countries draw four.

clues.title: Guardrail: white or red reflectors
text: Latvia has normal A-type guardrails with **white or red reflectors**.
NOTE: Estonia has no reflectors. Lithuania has orange reflectors. For a good overview of European guardrails, see [this infographic](/images/latvia/europeguardrail.png).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Normal A-type guardrails with white or red reflectors. Estonia has none, Lithuania uses orange.

clues.title: Language: letters with bars and hooks
text: **Latvian** belongs to the Baltic languages. The other major member of this branch is Lithuanian, to which it is closely related.
Within the Baltic languages, the following letters are unique to Latvian:
- Vowels with a macron (horizontal stripe): Ā Ē Ī.
- Consonants with a small hook: Ģ Ķ Ļ Ņ.
NOTE: Estonian is not a member of the Baltic languages(despite the name), and therefore looks significantly different.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Look for vowels with a bar on top (Ā Ē Ī) and consonants with a small hook (Ģ Ķ Ļ Ņ). Lithuanian is related; Estonian looks quite different.

differs.how: Related language but lacks these exact letters
Not a Baltic language, looks very different

clues.title: Language: street is "iela"
text: The Latvian word for street is **iela**. This word is unique to Latvian.
Very rarely, you might see ‘gatve’ in Riga (abbreviated as gat.). This word is also the standard word for street in Lithuania (usually abbreviated as g.).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The word for street is iela, which exists only here. Rarely, in the capital, you may see "gatve" (gat.), the standard Lithuanian word.

clues.title: House numbers: tall rectangles, many colours
text: Latvian house numbers are often shaped like **tall rectangles** and can be found in [several colours](https://www.google.com/maps/@56.6568307,23.7457261,3a,15y,38.74h,91.25t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sP7bXCAylAr5ghFSDKp9l1g!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
NOTE: This is not common in Estonia or Lithuania.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: House numbers are often tall rectangles in several colours. This is uncommon in Estonia and Lithuania.

clues.title: Houses: wood and white brick, steep metal roofs
text: Latvian architecture generally consists of a combination of **wood** and **white brick**, typically with somewhat steep **corrugated metal roofs**. Slightly modern houses with **pastel coloured stone walls** and houses with a combination of wood with another material, particularly white brick, are also common.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Wood and white brick houses with steep corrugated metal roofs. Newer ones may have pastel stone walls, and mixes of wood with white brick are common.

clues.title: Sign: blue direction sign, stylised arrow
text: Latvian directional signs are blue with white text.

NOTE: The arrow on Latvian signs is more stylized than in [Estonia](https://goo.gl/maps/eW7AJWdVriTfsprx7) and [Lithuania](https://goo.gl/maps/17A5xxGivFmbs4ae8), where the back part of the arrowhead is vertical.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Blue direction signs with white text. The arrowhead is more stylised than in Estonia and Lithuania, where the back of the arrowhead is vertical.

differs.how: Arrowhead has a vertical back edge
Arrowhead has a vertical back edge

clues.title: Google car: red Gen 4 car
text: A red generation 4 Google car can be found in Latvia.
NOTE: It can also be found in a few other European countries, including Lithuania, but not Estonia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A red Gen 4 Google car appears here. It also exists in a few other European countries, including Lithuania, but not Estonia.

clues.title: Google car: black Gen 4 car

NOTE: It can also be found in many other European countries, including Lithuania, but not Estonia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A black Gen 4 Google car appears here too. It is found in many European countries, including Lithuania, but not Estonia.

clues.title: Landscape: wide open fields, little forest
text: The area south of Jelgava is characterised by a **wide open landscape** with considerably less forest and more fields than most of the rest of Latvia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: South of one town, the land is open with far more fields and much less forest than the rest of the country.

clues.title: Houses: art nouveau old town
text: The historic downtown area of Riga is characterised by majestic [**art nouveau**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau)** architecture**, that is in places reminiscent of the architecture in Vienna. This is unique within Latvia, and even within the entire Baltics.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A historic city centre of grand art nouveau buildings, similar to Vienna in places. Unique in the whole Baltic region.

clues.title: Marker: electricity marker, black tip
text: You can find these electricity markers in Latvia — they have a distinct shape with a black tip and a different color underneath.

images.caption: Two short posts by the grass, one black with a white band and one yellow-topped, left and right

clues.summary: Electricity markers with a distinctive shape: a black tip over a different colour below.

clues.title: Vehicles: white buses and trams, blue bottom
text: Riga buses and trams are white with a blue bottom, VERY similar to the dutch ones.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Buses and trams in the capital are white with a blue lower half, very similar to the Dutch ones.
